New physics beyond the Standard Model can lead to extra matter effects on neutrino oscillation if the new interactions distinguish among the three flavors of neutrino. In Ref.1, we argued that a long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment in which the Fermilab-NUMI beam in its high-energy mode is aimed at the planned Hyper-Kamiokande detector would be capable of constraining the size of those extra matter effects, provided the vacuum value of \sin^2 2\theta_{23} is not too close to one. In this talk, we discuss how such a constraint would translate into limits on the coupling constants and masses of new particles in models such as topcolor assisted technicolor.

outputs.L2: Physics beyond the Standard Model may generate additional matter-induced effects in neutrino oscillations when the new interactions depend on neutrino flavor. In Ref. 1, we showed that these effects could be constrained by a long-baseline experiment directing the high-energy Fermilab NuMI beam toward the proposed Hyper-Kamiokande detector, as long as the vacuum value of \(\sin^2 2\theta_{23}\) is not very close to unity. outputs.L3:
Physics beyond the Standard Model could modify neutrino oscillations by generating additional matter effects, provided the new interactions distinguish among the three neutrino flavors. Such flavor-dependent interactions would alter the effective potential experienced by neutrinos as they propagate through matter, producing observable changes in their oscillation probabilities.

A long-baseline experiment using Fermilab’s high-energy NuMI neutrino beam directed toward the Hyper-Kamiokande detector could provide a sensitive probe of these nonstandard matter effects. The long propagation distance and high beam energy would enhance matter-induced modifications, allowing the experiment to place meaningful constraints on the strength of possible new flavor-dependent interactions.

The sensitivity of this approach would depend on the vacuum value of the atmospheric mixing parameter \(\sin^2 2\theta_{23}\). In particular, strong constraints could be obtained as long as this parameter is not too close to unity, corresponding to nearly maximal \(\nu_\mu\)-\(\nu_\tau\) mixing. Near maximal mixing, degeneracies can reduce the ability to distinguish nonstandard matter effects from the standard oscillation pattern.

Any resulting bounds on the additional matter potential could then be translated into constraints on the masses and coupling constants of hypothetical particles responsible for the new interactions. This would make long-baseline neutrino measurements relevant to specific theories beyond the Standard Model, including models such as topcolor-assisted technicolor.
outputs.L4:
Flavor-dependent physics beyond the Standard Model can modify neutrino propagation through matter. Unlike ordinary neutral-current interactions, which affect all active neutrino flavors equally and therefore contribute only an unobservable common phase, nonstandard interactions may generate different effective potentials for different flavors. These additional matter effects alter the effective mixing angles and oscillation frequencies, producing energy- and baseline-dependent changes in neutrino appearance and disappearance probabilities.

A particularly sensitive test could be obtained by directing the high-energy Fermilab NuMI beam toward the Hyper-Kamiokande detector in Japan. The exceptionally long baseline would force the beam to traverse a substantial portion of the Earth, allowing even relatively weak flavor-dependent interactions to accumulate into measurable distortions of the oscillation spectrum. Comparing neutrino and antineutrino data, and studying the energy dependence of the muon-neutrino survival probability, would help separate exotic matter effects from ordinary vacuum oscillations and standard matter effects.

The attainable sensitivity depends strongly on the atmospheric mixing angle \(\theta_{23}\). If the vacuum value of \(\sin^2 2\theta_{23}\) is sufficiently below unity, the nonmaximal flavor composition makes the oscillation probability more responsive to differences in the matter potentials experienced by muon and tau neutrinos. By contrast, when \(\theta_{23}\) is extremely close to maximal, some of the leading effects can be suppressed or become difficult to distinguish from shifts in the conventional oscillation parameters.

Such a long-baseline experiment could therefore place useful limits on flavor-nonuniversal neutrino interactions even if no statistically significant deviation from standard oscillations were observed. These phenomenological constraints could be translated into bounds on the couplings and masses of new particles that mediate the interactions. In models such as topcolor-assisted technicolor, for example, additional heavy gauge bosons can couple nonuniversally to fermion generations and induce extra neutrino matter potentials. NuMI-to-Hyper-Kamiokande measurements would consequently provide a complementary probe of these models, restricting combinations of new-particle masses and couplings that may be difficult to test through collider experiments alone.
outputs.L5:
### A New Standard Model

The New Standard Model represents a fresh approach to performance, reliability, and design. Built to meet evolving expectations, it combines proven principles with modern innovation. Its flexible structure makes it suitable for a wide range of applications, while its efficient operation helps reduce complexity and improve results.

More than an update, the New Standard Model establishes a benchmark for the future—one defined by quality, adaptability, and lasting value.

counterfactuals.output: Long-baseline neutrino experiments provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model through the energy- and baseline-dependent pattern of neutrino oscillations. This talk explores how current and next-generation data can constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions in matter, with emphasis on effective operators induced by new particles in topcolor-assisted technicolor models. We examine their impact on oscillation probabilities, parameter degeneracies, and CP-violation measurements, and discuss the complementary reach of experiments such as NOvA, T2K, DUNE, and Hyper-Kamiokande. The resulting limits connect neutrino oscillation observables to the masses and couplings of the underlying new particles.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a conference presentation abstract explaining how limits on extra neutrino matter effects can be translated into constraints on the masses and couplings of particles in models such as topcolor-assisted technicolor.
counterfactuals.output:
**From Neutrino Matter Effects to New-Particle Constraints in Topcolor-Assisted Technicolor**

Nonstandard neutrino interactions can modify neutrino propagation through matter by introducing additional flavor-dependent forward-scattering potentials. Experimental limits on these effects may therefore be recast as constraints on the mediators predicted by physics beyond the Standard Model. We present a general matching framework that connects bounds on matter-effect parameters, conventionally written as \(\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}^{fP}\), to the masses and couplings of new particles. For a heavy neutral mediator, such as the nonuniversal \(Z'\) boson appearing in topcolor-assisted technicolor, integrating out the mediator gives
\[
\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}^{fP}
\simeq
\frac{g_{\nu}^{\alpha\beta}g_{fP}}
{2\sqrt{2}\,G_F M_{Z'}^{2}},
\]
up to model-dependent charge assignments and normalization conventions. Consequently, an upper limit on \(|\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}^{fP}|\) becomes a lower bound on \(M_{Z'}/\sqrt{|g_{\nu}^{\alpha\beta}g_{fP}|}\), or, for a specified mass, an upper bound on the relevant coupling product.

We apply this procedure to representative topcolor-assisted technicolor scenarios, emphasizing the effects of generation-dependent charges, fermion mixing, and the proton, neutron, and electron composition of terrestrial matter. We also discuss the validity of the contact-interaction approximation and the complementarity of neutrino oscillation, coherent-scattering, electroweak, and collider constraints. This translation provides a systematic way to use neutrino matter effects as probes of heavy gauge sectors, including parameter regions that may be difficult to access through direct production alone.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write a short technical paragraph about constraining new flavor-dependent neutrino interactions with a long-baseline NuMI-to-Hyper-Kamiokande experiment?
counterfactuals.output: A hypothetical re-aimed NuMI-class beam from Fermilab to Hyper-Kamiokande, spanning roughly 9,000 km, would provide strong sensitivity to flavor-dependent neutrino nonstandard interactions (NSI) through enhanced matter effects. Such interactions modify the propagation Hamiltonian as \(V_{\alpha\beta}=\sqrt{2}G_F N_e(\delta_{\alpha e}\delta_{\beta e}+\epsilon_{\alpha\beta})\), producing energy- and flavor-dependent distortions in \(\nu_\mu\) disappearance and \(\nu_e\) appearance spectra. Joint neutrino and antineutrino measurements could constrain both diagonal flavor nonuniversality and off-diagonal NSI while helping resolve degeneracies with the mass ordering and CP phase. In practice, the existing NuMI beamline is not oriented toward Hyper-Kamiokande, so this would require a new or substantially redirected beam facility.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce an abstract that references earlier work showing that a high-energy Fermilab-NuMI beam aimed at Hyper-Kamiokande could constrain nonstandard neutrino matter effects unless vacuum \(\sin^2 2\theta_{23}\) is too close to unity, and state that the present talk interprets those bounds in specific beyond-Standard-Model theories.
counterfactuals.output: Earlier work showed that a high-energy Fermilab NuMI beam directed toward Hyper-Kamiokande could provide strong constraints on nonstandard neutrino matter effects, except when the vacuum value of \(\sin^2 2\theta_{23}\) lies too close to unity, where parameter degeneracies significantly reduce the sensitivity. In this talk, we reinterpret those model-independent bounds on matter-effect parameters within specific beyond-the-Standard-Model theories. We discuss how the projected constraints map onto mediator masses and couplings in representative ultraviolet-complete scenarios, and compare the resulting reach with complementary laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological limits.
